# Sewing Machine Oil vs. Silicone Spray for Window Channels

You are looking to replace a temporary fix with a durable solution for your sliding window mechanism. The core question is whether sewing machine oil can serve as a substitute for silicone-based lubricant in rubber channels, specifically regarding friction reduction and material compatibility. While both substances are liquids intended to reduce resistance between moving parts, their chemical compositions and physical properties diverge significantly. Using the wrong lubricant in an automotive environment often leads to accelerated wear rather than relief.

### The Mechanics of Friction in Rubber Channels

To understand why a specific lubricant matters, you must look at how friction works within a rubber seal. When a window moves, the rubber channel compresses against the glass and the metal guide rail. This creates high shear stress. If the surface is dry or contaminated with dust, the coefficient of friction spikes, causing the "stick-slip" phenomenon where the window feels like it's catching and releasing.

The goal is to introduce a layer that allows surfaces to slide smoothly without bonding together or degrading the surrounding materials. Silicone-based sprays are engineered for this specific purpose. They leave behind a dry film that provides low friction while resisting attraction to particulate matter like road dust. This "dry lubricity" is crucial because automotive windows operate in environments filled with abrasive grit.

### Why Sewing Machine Oil Fails in Automotive Applications

Sewing machine oil, often mistaken for engine oil due to its thick, dark viscosity, is chemically distinct from silicone or synthetic motor oils. It is typically a mineral oil blend containing zinc and other additives designed to protect steel gears in high-load sewing mechanisms.

The primary failure mode of using this oil on rubber is chemical incompatibility. Mineral oils contain hydrocarbon chains that interact poorly with polyurethane or EPDM rubber commonly found in automotive window seals. Over time, these solvents can cause the rubber to swell, soften, and eventually disintegrate. This process is known as plasticization. Once the structural integrity of the rubber channel degrades, it loses its ability to hold water away from the glass (hydrophobicity), leading to leaks and further corrosion of the door frame.

Furthermore, sewing machine oil lacks the anti-dust properties of silicone. As you noted in your experience, the initial improvement was followed by increased stickiness after a week. This is not because the oil "dried up" in the sense of evaporating; mineral oils do not evaporate. Instead, the oil acted as an adhesive, trapping dust and grit from the cleaned scissor railing and the interior door panel. This slurry creates a significantly higher coefficient of friction than dry silicone, effectively sanding the rubber channel and increasing drag on the glass.

### The Correct Lubrication Strategy

For a permanent fix on a 2008 Honda Civic or similar vehicle, you must revert to a silicone-based lubricant, specifically one labeled for automotive use. These products are formulated to penetrate tight tolerances in window regulators while repelling dirt.

When applying the lubricant, ensure the rubber channel is thoroughly cleaned first. Any residual grease from the previous engine oil application can prevent the new silicone film from adhering properly. Use a degreaser or brake cleaner on a lint-free cloth to remove all contaminants before spraying. Apply the silicone spray generously to both the inside of the rubber channel and the metal guide rail, then manually operate the window through its full range of motion to distribute the lubricant evenly.

If you are comfortable with DIY repairs, consider cleaning the scissor railing with a mild solvent to ensure no old debris remains before reassembly. The trade-off here is effort versus longevity; a few extra minutes of cleaning and using the correct chemical compound will prevent the recurrence of the sticky window issue without risking catastrophic seal failure.
